messages.subject: [statnet_help] Finding a predictive ergm
messages.body_plain:
Dear Gurus,

My goal is to choose (and justify the choice) a model
(including terms for individual differences, homophily, and closure)
giving the best prediction of ties to use in creating a predicted-tie 
network.
In the ergms I'm estimating, I find no clear favorite, and need help
to choose appropriately.

Sample ERGMs:
Model1 <- ergm(net ~ edges + nodefactor(foo) + nodematch(foo))
Model2 <- ergm(net ~ gwesp(fixed=F) + edges + nodefactor(foo) + 
nodematch(foo))
Model3 <- ergm(net ~ gwesp(fixed=F) + edges + nodefactor(foo) + 
nodematch(foo), theta0=c(0,Model1$coef))
 
Model1
Pro: no MCMC / precise SEs,  non-degenerate
Con: no closure term, terrible GOF

Model2
Pro: much better GOF, AIC & BIC < Model1
Con: degenerate, suspect standard errors

Model3
Pro: non-degenerate, much better GOF
Con: AIC & BIC more than twice those of Model1

Since my goal is prediction and not hypothesis testing,
wouldn't Model2 be best even with the degeneracy?
Does degeneracy affect confidence in coefficient point estimates in 
addition to SEs?
If degenerate models should not be used predictively,
Model2 is better in terms of GOF, but horrible in terms of AIC & BIC.
I'd prefer to stick with models with good GOF,
but the huge increases in AIC & BIC give me pause.

Alternatively, are there other things I should be doing in structuring 
my ergms to reduce the likelihood of degeneracy?

Thanks very much for your help and advice!
Best,
Brian

-- 
Brian Rubineau
Assistant Professor, Organizational Behavior       146K Ives Hall
School of Industrial and Labor Relations         ph. 607.255.3048
Cornell University                              fax. 810.963.2738
Ithaca, NY 14853                            brubineau@cornell.edu

messages.subject: [statnet_help] problem with cug.test
messages.body_plain:
In using a function I've written to compute the Watts-Strogatz
clustering coefficient, I get different observed values when using it
in cug.test versus using it alone.

g = rgraph(10)
clusteringCoefficientWS(g) # see function below
[1] 0.4638095
cug = cug.test( g, FUN = clusteringCoefficientWS, mode = "graph",
cmode = "edges" )
cug

Univariate Conditional Uniform Graph Test

Conditioning Method: edges
Graph Type: graph
Diagonal Used: FALSE
Replications: 1000

Observed Value: 0.431746
Pr(X>=Obs): 0.748
Pr(X<=Obs): 0.252

# Function:
clusteringCoefficientWS = function( g ) {
	total = 0
	nodesUsed = 0
	for( iteration in 1:length( g[1,] ) )  {
		# Retrieve the ego network
		egonetwork = ego.extract( g, iteration, neighborhood = "combined" )
		# If ego has neighbors, calculate the clustering coefficient for this node
		if ( dim( egonetwork[[1]] )[1] < 3 ) {
			# Clustering coefficient is undefined
			next
		} else {
			# Get the neighbor network ( ego is the first row/col )
			neighbornetwork =
					egonetwork[[1]][ 	2:nrow( egonetwork[[1]] ),
										2:ncol( egonetwork[[1]] ) ]
			# Get the degree of ego
			degree = nrow( neighbornetwork )
			# Get the number of edges
			numEdges = sum( upperTriangle( neighbornetwork , diag = FALSE ) )
			C_i = numEdges / ( degree * ( degree - 1 ) / 2 )
			total = total + C_i
			nodesUsed = nodesUsed + 1
		}
	}
	clusCoef = total / nodesUsed
	return( clusCoef )
}


Brian Riordan
Postdoctoral Fellow
Department of Psychological and Brain Sciences
Indiana University

messages.subject: [statnet_help] Error: package 'networksis' required by 'statnet' could not be found
messages.subject_clean: [statnet_help] Error: package 'networksis' required by 'statnet' could not be found
messages.body_plain:
Hi Jenine,

"networksis" is not available for Windows (under R 2.9.1) due to a mismatch
with one of the packages it depends on. However, "ergm" does not depend on
"networksis", so I would suggest installing "ergm" instead of "statnet" and
you will have all the functionality you likely need.

If you actually need "networksis" itself, I can email you a version of it.

Cheers,

Mark

for the "statnet" Team
